title: Market Wages and Youth Crime
key_finding: Canonical individual-level test: legal wages compete with criminal earnings for youth time; higher legal wages predict less property crime. Wages explain a substantial share of the property-crime decline among youth in the late 1980s.
effect_direction: negative (higher wage -> less youth property crime)

title: Youth Crime and the Minimum Wage
key_finding: Entry exists in Crossref-linked record; minimum-wage compression of the youth wage tail is the mechanism channeling Grogger-style wage-crime results. Abstract not retrievable in this scan - magnitude unverified.

title: Do Minimum Wage Increases Reduce Crime?
key_finding: Modern minimum-wage-crime test; reported modest reductions in property crime in some specifications; not established as a robust literature-wide finding.
effect_direction: negative (property) in some specs; not robust

title: Labor Market Concentration, Minimum Wages, and Local Property Crime Rates
key_finding: New frontier paper linking monopsony (labor-market concentration) + minimum wages to local property crime; too new for citations.
basis_of_estimate: local labor-market concentration x minimum wage

title: Minimum Wage and Crime: Evidence from China
key_finding: Non-US minimum-wage-crime test exists (China); magnitude not captured in scan.

title: Impact of the minimum wage increase on intimate partner violence (IPV): a quasi-experimental study
venue: Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health
key_finding: Min-wage increases affect IPV - wage policy as violence-prevention lever; direction favorable (reduction) per quasi-experimental design.

authors: J Interpersonal Violence 2023; Child Abuse & Neglect 2025
title: The Impact of Increased Minimum Wage on Child Neglect Varies by Developmental Age (plus: US state minimum wages and maltreatment-related child deaths, 2025)
key_finding: Minimum-wage policy reduces child neglected/maltreatment outcomes - wage floors improve at-home civic outcomes, strongest on neglect.
effect_direction: negative (higher min wage -> less neglect/maltreatment death)

title: The impact of temporary assistance for needy families, minimum wage, and Earned Income Tax Credit on child maltreatment
key_finding: Bundle of wage-support policies (TANF, min wage, EITC) and maltreatment; EITC/min-wage generosity associated with lower maltreatment.

authors: Gould ED, Weinberg BA, Mustard DB
title: Crime Rates and Local Labor Market Opportunities in the United States: 1979-1997
venue: Review of Economics and Statistics (REStat 2002; 1998 WP record)
key_finding: Falling wages/employment for less-skilled men explain a meaningful share of rising unskilled-property crime through the 1980s-90s; labor-market variables move crime even with controls.
effect_direction: negative (better low-skill labor markets -> less property crime)

title: Crime and Economic Incentives
venue: Journal of the European Economic Association (record)
key_finding: UK evidence: crime rates fall when real wages of low-paid men rise at the bottom of the wage distribution; the wage-crime relationship is concentrated at the bottom tail, not the middle/median.

title: Crime and Economic Incentives
key_finding: Authoritative review: labor-market conditions matter for crime, with elasticities concentrated in property crime; violent-crime responses are smaller and less consistent。
effect_direction: review: negative for property; ~null/small for violent

title: Work and Crime
key_finding: Handbook synthesis of work-crime nexus: employment/earnings opportunity costs are the dominant mechanism for property crime.

title: Crime and the labor market
key_finding: Latest handbook synthesis of labor-market-crime causal evidence; confirms elasticities small per-point but economically meaningful for property crime; weak violent-crime effects.

title: The Effect of Deindustrialization on Local Economies: Evidence from New England Textile Towns
key_finding: Direct deindustrialization effect measured on local economies, not on crime; the crime-side magnitude for US deindustrialization is NOT well identified in the indexed peer literature - a gap, not an established effect size.

title: Economic Cynicism, COVID-19 and Deaths of Despair in Rural Ohio Counties
key_finding: Civic-side outcome (deaths of despair) responds to local economic decline/cynicism - extends mid-band 'wage decline' outcomes beyond crime.

title: The illegal market for sex in the United States: Insights from economic research
key_finding: High-earnings illegal markets ('crime as a premium-wage substitute'): criminalization pushes premium-wage illegal markets underground and raises attendant violence; direct high-wage-employment-crime estimates remain scarce.

title: Immigrants, Legal Status, and Illegal Trade
key_finding: High-skill/geography-specific legal-status effects on illegal trade participation; specialized-band evidence is heterogeneous and status-, not wage-, driven.

title: Hidden Costs of Ban the Box Laws: Unraveling the Effects on Drug-Related Deaths
key_finding: Employment barriers (criminal-history checks) have spillover costs (drug-related deaths) - restricting access to legal employment raises harms; specialized-band causal lever.

title: Post-prison Employment Quality and Future Criminal Justice Contact
key_finding: EMPLOYMENT QUALITY (not just any job) predicts lower future criminal-justice contact after prison; the quality/marginal-wage channel is what binds.

title: Crime, Search, and Ex-offenders' Accessibility to Labor Markets
key_finding: Search-friction model: geographic accessibility to jobs lowers re-offense incentives; employment access is a crime lever with local-geography structure.

title: Are we failing young people not in employment, education or training (NEETs)? A systematic review and meta-analysis
key_finding: 18 RCT/quasi-RCT trials for NEET interventions; employment outcomes improve modestly; secondary outcomes include health/welfare, not recidivism - specialized-band employment programs show small average employment effects.
effect_direction: positive (small employment gains); recidivism not primary

title: Identifying the Effect of Unemployment on Crime
key_finding: Instrumented unemployment (defense-spending shifts, alcohol-cycle controls) yields LARGE positive effects of unemployment on the seven felony offenses; magnitudes larger than naive OLS; property crime dominates.

title: Does Unemployment Increase Crime? Evidence from U.S. Data 1974-2000
key_finding: Unemployment raises PROPERTY crime (strong, procyclical); effects on VIOLENT crime are small or null - the band's core stratification fact: employment effects are property-crime specific.

title: Does unemployment increase crime? Evidence from Italian provinces
key_finding: Non-US replication: unemployment-crime link present for property offenses across Italian provinces.

title: Unemployment and crime: Experimental evidence of the causal effects of intensified ALMPs on crime rates
key_finding: ALMP intensification (quasi-random) shifted crime among the unemployed - the first direct experimental labor-market-program-to-crime test; effects concentrated in property crime.
effect_direction: mixed (program pushes job search, displaces crime)

title: Summer jobs reduce violence among disadvantaged youth
key_finding: Rochester/Boston/Philadelphia-style summer youth jobs (One Summer Chicago): RCT - violent-crime arrests fell ~33-43% over the treatment summer; effects driven by VIOLENT arrests, not property.
effect_direction: negative (big violent-crime arrest drop during program)

authors: Gelber A, Isen A, Kessler JB
title: Rethinking the Benefits of Youth Employment Programs: The Heterogeneous Effects of Summer Jobs
key_finding: Follow-up: summer-jobs effects are heterogeneous - largest for youth most at risk (school-engagement/behavior margins), small for average participants; explains null earnings and positive crime/behavior results.
effect_direction: negative for at-risk youth (violent arrests); ~null average earnings

title: The Effects of Youth Employment: Evidence from New York City Summer Youth Employment Program Lotteries
key_finding: NYC SYEP lotteries: small earnings gains; reductions in incarcerations/arrests for some subgroups; magnitude smaller than Chicago's violent-arrest effects.

title: More than a Job: Final Results from the Evaluation of the Center for Employment Opportunities (CEO) Transitional Jobs Program
key_finding: RCT of transitional jobs for former prisoners: modest early effects on employment/arrests, NOT sustained at long follow-up; recidivism effects null overall - transitional jobs alone do not durably cut recidivism.

title: Examining the effects of a transitional employment program for formerly incarcerated people on employment and recidivism
key_finding: Recent RCT of transitional employment for formerly incarcerated: employment effects present; recidivism improvements limited - consistent with CEO null pattern.

title: Putting employment-based reentry programs into context (and: Why the risk-and-need principles are relevant even to employment programs)
key_finding: Framework papers: employment-program effects on recidivism are strongest when programs target high-risk-need clients; generic job programs underperform - targeting is the moderator.

title: Evaluating the Benefits and Costs of the Job Corps
venue: Journal of Policy Analysis and Management
key_finding: Job Corps benefit-cost: positive social returns; long-run follow-ups (NBER) show modest education/earnings gains with mixed crime results (property-crime reductions in some cohorts).

title: Predicting and Preventing Gun Violence: An Experimental Evaluation of READI Chicago
key_finding: RCT N=2,456 men at very high risk: 18-month paid transitional job + CBT + supports. PRIMARY violent index: no statistically significant effect. Shooting/homicide ARRESTS fell 65% (p=0.13 after adjustment). Control-group victimization 11 per 100 - the highest-bar employment-plus-therapy test to date.

title: Examining the work-crime association in emerging adulthood: A longitudinal analysis based on a Dutch population register
key_finding: Population-register longitudinal: more work hours associate with less crime in emerging adulthood; direction consistent, causality unproven at individual level.

title: Does Stricter Child Support Enforcement Create More Criminal Dads?
key_finding: Counter-channel: stricter enforcement (higher effective wage tax on noncustodial fathers) can raise crime among low-income fathers - wage-policy design matters for the crime side.
effect_direction: harmful-by-design (enforcement -> more father crime, some specs)

title: Welfare Payments and Crime
key_finding: Cash-arrival timing: violent/property crime falls in the days right after monthly welfare/SSI disbursement and rises at cash exhaustion - income level AND liquidity timing both move crime.
effect_direction: negative (payment arrival -> less crime; exhaustion -> more)

title: Welfare payments, food stamps, and crime: evidence from US county-level data
venue: International Journal of Public Law and Policy
key_finding: County-level food-stamp generosity associates with lower crime; smaller magnitude than Foley's timing effect.

title: Is the Social Safety Net a Long-Term Investment? Large-Scale Evidence From the Food Stamps Rollout
key_finding: 17.5M Americans: pre-age-5 food-stamp access -> 0.5pp LOWER incarceration as adults, +1.2yr life expectancy (civic outcomes decades later) - wage/output transfers to families are long-run crime-prevention.

title: The Impact of Living-Wage Ordinances on Urban Crime
venue: Industrial Relations: A Journal of Economy and Society
key_finding: Living-wage ordinances (city-level wage floors) associated with lower urban (property) crime; magnitude modest and identification debated.

title: Effects of Welfare Reform on Women's Crime
key_finding: Welfare-to-work reform effects on women's offending are mixed: employment pushes can RAISE low-grade property/entry offenses for unconverted workfare recipients - wage-output design (carrot vs. mandate) determines sign.

title: Does a Higher Income Have Positive Health Effects? Using the Earned Income Tax Credit to Explore the Income-Health Gradient
key_finding: EITC-induced income improves health (proxy civic outcome); direct EITC-crime magnitudes are NOT well-identified in indexed peer literature - a named gap for the wage-output band.

title: Investigating the Poverty-Reducing Effects of SNAP on Non-nutritional Family Outcomes
key_finding: SNAP improves 5 family-stress-model domains incl. child behavior/dev and abuse-neglect - wage-output transfers improve civic/family outcomes systematically.
